overview.title: Czech State Finances at a Glance

expenses.title: Expenditures
expenses.subtitle: Where public money goes — mandatory and discretionary state expenditure.
expenses.dynamicSubtitle: How the state spends {{amount}} bn CZK annually
expenses.introText: State budget expenditure is divided into mandatory spending — legally required payments such as pensions and debt repayments — and discretionary spending, which the government decides each year when approving the budget. Total expenditure grows with the economy, but also with demographic shifts and changing political priorities.

descriptions.socialProtection: Legally mandated benefits — old-age and disability pensions, family support and unemployment assistance.
descriptions.healthcare: State-budget contribution to healthcare — primarily payments for state-insured persons to health insurers.
descriptions.education: Funding for schools, universities and research — teacher salaries, grants and scholarships.
descriptions.defenseAndSecurity: Expenditure on the armed forces, police, fire services and intelligence agencies.
descriptions.transport: Construction and maintenance of roads, motorways, railways and water infrastructure.
descriptions.debtService: Interest payments on government bonds and principal repayments on state loans.
descriptions.publicAdministration: Operation of ministries, parliament, the presidency and the judiciary.
descriptions.municipalTransfers: Transfers and grants to municipalities and regions — shared taxes and targeted subsidies.
descriptions.environmentAndAgriculture: Support for agriculture, forestry and rural development; environmental protection and nature conservation.
descriptions.cultureAndSport: Funding for theatres, museums, cultural heritage, sport and physical activity.
descriptions.industryAndEconomy: Support for industry, energy transition, business subsidies and export promotion.

incomes.title: Revenue
incomes.subtitle: How the state funds its budget — tax and non-tax revenues.
incomes.dynamicSubtitle: How the state collects {{amount}} bn CZK annually
incomes.introText: State budget revenues consist primarily of tax receipts — VAT, income taxes and excise duties — and social security contributions. Total revenue changes annually depending on economic growth, changes in tax rates and employment levels.

descriptions.vat: Value Added Tax is the primary indirect tax. It is collected at the point of sale of goods and services.
descriptions.incomeTax: Includes personal and corporate income taxes. Rates vary by income type.
descriptions.socialInsurance: Social insurance contributions are paid by both employers and employees. They fund pensions, sick pay and unemployment benefits.
descriptions.exciseDuties: Excise duties apply to motor fuels, alcohol, tobacco and energy products.
descriptions.euTransfers: Grants and transfers received from the EU budget, primarily structural and cohesion funds.
descriptions.otherRevenue: Other revenues include fees, property income and state-owned enterprise dividends.

landing.headline: Do you know where your taxes go?
landing.subheadline: Each year the Czech state collects over 2 trillion CZK. See how it's spent — revenues, expenditures and deficit for 2018–2025.
landing.feature1Q: How does the state manage its finances?
landing.feature1Body: A complete view of revenues, expenditures and deficit with trends from 2020.
landing.feature2Body: 8 categories of mandatory and discretionary spending — from pensions to defence.
landing.feature3Q: How does the state pay for it all?
landing.feature3Body: VAT, income taxes, social security contributions and other sources of state revenue.
landing.aboutBody: Data is sourced from state final accounts and budget acts for 2018–2025, published by the Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic.
landing.footerCtaBody: Open the interactive state budget overview and find out where your taxes go.

subcategoryDescriptions.oldAgePensions: Basic old-age pension paid to individuals who have reached retirement age and met the required insurance period.
subcategoryDescriptions.disabilityPensions: Disability pensions for individuals whose health condition significantly limits their ability to work.
subcategoryDescriptions.familySupport: Child benefits, parental allowance and other social payments supporting families with children.
subcategoryDescriptions.unemploymentBenefits: Unemployment support for individuals who have lost their job and are registered with the employment office.
subcategoryDescriptions.socialServices: Funding for care homes, day care centres and field social services.
subcategoryDescriptions.hospitalCare: Reimbursement of inpatient care — hospitalisation, surgery and specialist treatment.
subcategoryDescriptions.primaryCare: Outpatient treatment by general practitioners and specialists without hospitalisation.
subcategoryDescriptions.medications: State subsidy for medicines and medical devices prescribed to patients.
subcategoryDescriptions.emergencyServices: Operation of emergency medical services and trauma centres.
subcategoryDescriptions.primarySecondarySchools: Funding for primary and secondary schools — teacher salaries, buildings and teaching materials.
subcategoryDescriptions.universities: Subsidies to public universities for teaching, research and operations.
subcategoryDescriptions.researchDevelopment: Grants and institutional support for scientific research at academies and research institutes.
subcategoryDescriptions.vocationalTraining: Funding for vocational schools, retraining courses and practical instruction.
subcategoryDescriptions.armedForces: Salaries of professional soldiers, procurement of equipment and combat training.
subcategoryDescriptions.police: Operation of the Czech Police and other security forces maintaining public order.
subcategoryDescriptions.intelligence: Funding for BIS, Military Intelligence and other intelligence agencies.
subcategoryDescriptions.roads: Construction and repair of motorways, Class-I roads and bridges.
subcategoryDescriptions.railways: Investment in the rail network, purchase of rolling stock and track repairs.
subcategoryDescriptions.publicTransit: Subsidies for public transport — buses, metro and suburban services.
subcategoryDescriptions.waterManagement: Construction and maintenance of dams, flood protection measures and water supply infrastructure.
subcategoryDescriptions.bondInterest: Interest paid to holders of government bonds issued to finance budget deficits.
subcategoryDescriptions.loanServicing: Principal and interest repayments on state loans and credits.
subcategoryDescriptions.ministries: Expenditure on the operations and staffing of individual government departments.
subcategoryDescriptions.localGovernments: Contributions to regions, municipalities and their offices for delegated state administration.
subcategoryDescriptions.parliament: Expenditure on the Chamber of Deputies, the Senate, the Presidential Office and their staffs.
subcategoryDescriptions.judiciary: Funding for courts, the public prosecutor's office and the prison service.
subcategoryDescriptions.environment: Expenditure on nature conservation, air quality and waste management.
subcategoryDescriptions.agriculture: Subsidies to farmers, rural development support and funding of agricultural research.
subcategoryDescriptions.culture: Funding for theatres, museums, public-service media and cultural heritage.
subcategoryDescriptions.sport: Public support for sports, physical activity and leisure activities.
subcategoryDescriptions.standardRateGoods: VAT collected on goods and services taxed at the standard rate of 21%.
subcategoryDescriptions.reducedRateGoods: VAT on goods and services at the reduced rate of 12% — food, medicines, books.
subcategoryDescriptions.importVat: VAT collected on goods imported from outside the EU at the border.
subcategoryDescriptions.personalIncomeTax: Tax on wages, business income and other income of individuals.
subcategoryDescriptions.corporateIncomeTax: Tax on corporate profits at the rate of 21%.
subcategoryDescriptions.withholdingTax: Withholding tax on dividends, interest and royalties.
subcategoryDescriptions.pensionInsurance: Mandatory contributions funding the pay-as-you-go pension system.
subcategoryDescriptions.healthInsurance: Mandatory contributions paid by employers and employees for healthcare.
subcategoryDescriptions.sicknessInsurance: Contributions funding sickness benefits and maternity allowance.
subcategoryDescriptions.fuelExcise: Excise duty on petrol, diesel and other motor fuels.
subcategoryDescriptions.tobaccoExcise: Excise duty on cigarettes, cigars and other tobacco products.
subcategoryDescriptions.alcoholExcise: Excise duty on spirits, beer and wine.
subcategoryDescriptions.energyTaxes: Taxes on electricity, natural gas and solid fuels.
subcategoryDescriptions.euTransfers: Received grants and structural funds from the European Union budget.
subcategoryDescriptions.dividendsAndProfits: Income from state stakes in state-owned enterprises and financial institutions.
subcategoryDescriptions.administrativeFees: Fees for administrative acts — issuing documents, permits and licences.
subcategoryDescriptions.propertyIncome: Revenues from leasing state property and selling real estate.
subcategoryDescriptions.stateInsureesContribution: Contributions paid to health insurers on behalf of state-insured persons — children, pensioners, the unemployed and others.
subcategoryDescriptions.publicHealth: Expenditure on public health protection, epidemiology, hygiene services and disease prevention.
subcategoryDescriptions.regionalGrants: Targeted subsidies and investment grants transferred to regions and municipalities.
subcategoryDescriptions.sharedTaxRevenues: Portion of national tax revenues redistributed to local governments under the fiscal equalisation system.
subcategoryDescriptions.waterResources: Construction and maintenance of water reservoirs, flood defences and water supply networks.
subcategoryDescriptions.energyAndClimate: Support for the energy sector, renewable energy transition and climate-related investment.
subcategoryDescriptions.businessSupport: Grants and subsidies supporting business investment, innovation and SME development.
subcategoryDescriptions.tradeAndExport: Funding for export promotion agencies, trade missions and international economic cooperation.
subcategoryDescriptions.euStructuralFunds: Drawdowns from EU Structural Funds for regional development and economic cohesion.
subcategoryDescriptions.euCohesionFund: Drawdowns from the EU Cohesion Fund for transport and environmental infrastructure.
subcategoryDescriptions.employmentPolicyContrib: Contributions financing active employment policy measures, retraining and job placement services.
